name: Cha ca
summary: Quy Nhon's tuna fish cake, fried until chewy and crisp or steamed with a thin yellow egg layer. It is the same cake that goes into bún chả cá.
origin: Quy Nhon. The noodle bowl built on this cake uses a broth of tuna bone and head.
texture: The provincial portal says the fried cake is smooth, soft, and chewy without being too fatty, and the steamed cake is the plainer of the two.
taste: Pepper heat and the sweetness of the fish. The broth it goes into is clear, scented with grilled shallot and rock sugar, and some kitchens add bamboo shoot and straw mushroom. Some cooks add scallion and dill to the cake. Others leave the dill out.
howToEat: Eat the steamed cake hot with chili sauce and a few herb leaves, or order it inside bún chả cá.
where: Quy Nhon. For the noodle bowl, go to Nguyễn Huệ.
seoTitle: Cha ca — Quy Nhon tuna cake
seoDescription: Quy Nhon chả cá is a tuna cake, fried chewy and crisp or steamed with a thin egg layer, and the cake inside bún chả cá.
